findings.claim: The script uses the BSD/macOS-only `sed -i '' -E` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux). When it fails, the .env update does not happen but the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated.

findings.claim: After the deleteCache mutation in CredentialActionsDropdown succeeds, it only calls onSuccess and does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. Callers that pass no onSuccess, such as EventAdvancedTab, then show a stale cacheUpdatedAt / 'Last updated'.

verifier.reason: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50, deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.() without invalidating viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike disconnectMutation at lines 61-64). Because packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without passing onChanged (forwarded as onSuccess at packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:75,125,183), the query at line 157 is never invalidated and keeps showing a stale cacheUpdatedAt.

findings.claim: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with empty data. With updateMany in Prisma 5.4.2 this does not bump @updatedAt, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and the call adds an extra UPDATE on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run.

verifier.reason: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1023-1024 calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) (defined at packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405 via prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany), which with empty data in Prisma ^5.4.2 (packages/prisma/package.json:27-30) does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:860). Moreover, cache status reads CalendarCache.updatedAt (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:154-168, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-36) rather than SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, making this updateMany call unnecessary work on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run.

findings.claim: The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, which ignores the user's locale (i18n.language from useLocale) and profile timezone.

verifier.reason: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-94, the cache_last_updated timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }), ignoring i18n.language from useLocale() (line 37) and omitting any timeZone option for the user's profile timezone.

findings.claim: dev:cron switches from ts-node to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared as a dependency and is not in yarn.lock. npx therefore downloads it from the registry at run time.

verifier.reason: apps/web/package.json:11 defines dev:cron as "npx tsx cron-tester.ts", while tsx is not declared in apps/web/package.json (only ts-node and typescript appear at lines 196-197) or root package.json (lines 85-125). yarn.lock likewise has no tsx entry (jumping directly from tsutils at yarn.lock:45185 to tty-browserify at yarn.lock:45196), so npx downloads tsx from the npm registry at run time.

findings.claim: prisma.credential.findFirst has no select, so it loads the full Credential row, including the key (OAuth tokens), only to check existence and ownership.

verifier.reason: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-26, prisma.credential.findFirst omits a select clause, loading the entire Credential row including its key JSON column (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222-226). The returned credential object is only checked with if (!credential) on line 24 to verify existence and ownership and is never used afterward.

findings.claim: The mock getCacheStatusByCredentialIds does not accept the credentialIds parameter, so it does not match the interface signature.

verifier.reason: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27 defines async getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() with no parameters, whereas packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts:30-32 declares getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds: number[]). Although TypeScript allows implementing an interface method with fewer parameters and all other methods in CalendarCacheRepositoryMock omit parameters the same way, the mock's own signature does not accept credentialIds.
